results.content: # Refinement of Boundary Regression Using Uncertainty in Temporal Action Localization. Boundary localization is a key component of most temporal action localization frameworks for untrimmed video. However, natural ambiguity exists for labeling an accurate action boundaries with such datasets. In this paper, we propose a method to model this uncertainty. Specifically, we construct a Gaussian model for predicting the uncertainty variance of the boundary. For most existing one- and two-stage frameworks, more accurate boundaries and reliable proposals can be obtained without additional computation. For the one-stage decoupled singleshot temporal action detection (Decouple-SSAD) [11] framework, we first apply the adaptive pyramid feature fusion method to fuse its features of different scales and optimize its structure. Then, we introduce the uncertainty based method and improve state-of-the-art mAP@0.5 value from 37.9% to 41.6% on THUMOS14. Moreover, for the two-stage proposalproposal interaction through a graph convolutional network (PGCN) [33], with such uncertainty method, we also gain significant improvements on both THUMOS14 and ActivityNet v1.3 datasets.

results.title: Active Contour Models: Image Segmentation & Boundary Detection
results.content: # Active Contour Models (Snakes): Unraveling the Secrets of Image Segmentation and Boundary Detection Imagine a world without computers that can perceive and understand images! One remarkable technique that has stood the test of time is the Active Contour Model, affectionately known as “snakes.” In this article, we delve into the depths of snakes and explore how they gracefully dance through images, seeking and capturing object boundaries with precision. Just like snakes can adapt their shape and form to the environment’s contours, these models aimed to do the same for objects in images. ### Active Contour Models: Mastering Object Boundary Detection In the previous section, we introduced the enigmatic concept of active contour models, known as “snakes,” and explored their elegant dance toward accurate image segmentation. ### Deep Learning Takes the Stage: A Symphony of Image Segmentation with Neural Networks In the previous sections, we explored the captivating world of active contour models (snakes) and accurate image segmentation. ### Active Contour Models and Deep Learning Unite In the previous sections, we marveled at the elegance of active contour models (snakes) and the symphony of deep learning-based segmentation techniques. #### The Power of Fusion: Combining Snakes and CNNs Active contour models and deep learning techniques complement each other, compensating for their limitations. #### Hybrid Approaches: Fusion One common fusion technique involves employing active contour models to refine the segmentation results obtained from deep learning models. The deep learning model captures global context, while the active contour model focuses on local details, resulting in more precise segmentations. This process leverages the pre-learned features, saving time and computational resources, while the active contour model refines the segmentation for the specific medical domain. This augments the fusion of active contour models and deep learning techniques, resulting in more robust and accurate segmentation. #### Beyond Image Segmentation The relationship between active contour models and deep learning extends beyond image segmentation, showcasing their versatility in various computer vision tasks. For instance, combining active contour models with Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) opens up new possibilities for image synthesis with precise object boundaries. Active contour models and their robustness and real-time performance synergize with deep learning and its ability to learn intricate patterns and features.

results.content: # Boundary Network. Here, boundary nodes are those occupying critical positions in the network graph that define the network's physical or logical boundary. Distributed boundary detection algorithms enable nodes to identify themselves as boundary nodes using only local neighbor information, which is essential for network services such as routing and coverage verification. Distributed boundary detection (DBD) algorithms allow each node in a network to determine its status as a boundary node using information from its three-hop neighbors, without requiring explicit node location or distance data. In peer models, two networks independently process data, while network boundary nodes map information between networks to enable data transmission. In sensor networks, strategies for boundary identification include building shortest path trees and identifying cut nodes through network flooding, which are then used to determine the network boundary. Boundary-network nodes serve as critical intermediaries that map information between two networks, enabling each network to independently process data within its own structure while facilitating data transmission across boundaries. The concept of boundary networks spans practical applications in network security and access control, theoretical models in distributed systems and graph theory, and computational geometry algorithms for boundary evaluation. Future research directions include enhancing boundary detection algorithms to better handle dynamic and mobile environments, improving the efficiency of remediation processes in security architectures, and advancing data structure representations to support complex network topologies and geometries.
